subject: Post-call: Alpha proof scoping & success signals
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya@crestline.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-04T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Alpha proof scoping & success signals

Hi Maya — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to iterate. I attached a one-page scope and a sample prompt set (see attachments).

Recap (from our discussion):
- Goal: run an "Alpha proof" (2-week sandbox) to validate behavior of Redwood inference for Crestline's knowledge-augmented summarization pipeline.
- Primary constraints: P95 latency and cost per token are the gating signals for production readiness; quality measures are domain extraction accuracy and hallucination rate.
- Stakeholders: Product (Maya), Platform/Procurement (procurement@crestline.ai), Redwood: Soojin (sales), Ben (solutions), Karthik (SRE).

Proposed success signals (high-level):
- Latency: P95 end-to-end inference <= 180 ms at 50 concurrent users (measured from API entry to token stream start).
- Throughput: sustain 200 requests/sec with <5% tail latency increase during a 15-min soak.
- Cost: average model cost <= $0.0025 / token (accounting for batching & KV cache).
- Quality: domain extraction F1 >= 0.88 on the benchmark prompt set; hallucination rate <= 3% measured against the labeled sample set.

Evaluation plan (two-week alpha sandbox):
Week 0 (prep, alignment): confirm sample dataset, red-team prompt list, and measurement hooks.
Week 1 (soak + smoke): run steady-state soak for 6 hours, capture latency/throughput/cost; run automated quality evals.
Week 2 (edge cases + hand eval): run adversarial prompt set, manual review for hallucination cases, finalize readout.

Owners (initial):
- Redwood: Ben (test harness + metrics instrumentation), Karthik (deployment profile, quantization advisory), Soojin (project owner / commercial cadence).
- Crestline: Maya (product), procurement@crestline.ai (contract & PO).

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Maya: confirm the two-week sandbox window and procurement contact.
2) Ben: can you review the attached scope and call out any missing measurement hooks?
3) Karthik: we need a recommended instance profile and expected cost range so Crestline procurement can provision budget.

Attachments: crestline_alpha_scope.xlsx (scope & timeline), crestline_sample_prompts.jsonl (anonymized sample prompts).

If this looks right I’ll propose wizarded kickoff dates (Oct 12 or Oct 19) and draft a mutual action plan.

Thanks —
Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
From: Maya Patel <maya@crestline.ai>

Thanks Soojin — useful summary. Procurement is now CC'd. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The latency KPI is measured end-to-end, but include the 3rd-party retrieval step (we will provide a mock retrieval endpoint for the alpha).
- On cost, can you show modeled examples with and without KV caching enabled? Our finance team wants to understand the upside from caching.
- For quality, we will supply the labeled benchmark for extraction tasks (approx. 1,200 labeled items). We'll also want a short list of acceptance examples (5-10) that must be passed manually.

We can do Oct 12 kickoff, but procurement will need an SOW/quote to approve the sandbox spend. Can Redwood provide a 2-week trial quote and a short SOW?

Maya
Product Lead, Crestline AI
maya@crestline.ai

Thanks — added a few concrete measurement hooks and a suggested harness below. I also attached an internal checklist of tests I’ll run.

Proposed measurement instrumentation (summary):
- Latency: instrument both client-side (synthetic runner) and server-side (request-queue delta + model token start). Report P50/P95/P99 and 95th tail over sliding 15-min windows.
- Throughput: run a 15-min soak at target RPS then a 2-hour stress ramp to find degradation point.
- Cost/token: snapshot cost with the following variants: baseline model (FP16) vs quantized int8 vs caching-enabled.
- Quality: run automated extraction eval returning precision/recall/F1; run a small manual pass (10 docs) flagged by Crestline for high-risk content.

Acceptance gates (detailed):
- Gate A (smoke): P95 <= 250 ms, extraction F1 >= 0.80, cost/token <= $0.004.
- Gate B (alpha pass): P95 <= 180 ms, extraction F1 >= 0.88, hallucination <= 3%, sustained throughput 200 req/s with <10% latency degradation.

Test harness & artifacts I’ll deliver:
- synthetic_load_runner.tar.gz (load profiles, runner config)
- measurement_report_<date>.csv (raw samples)
- bench_summary.pdf (dashboard-ready summary)

Tentative timeline if we kickoff Oct 12:
- Oct 12 (Day 0): Environment setup, shared dataset ingest.
- Oct 13–14: Smoke & soak runs.
- Oct 15–17: Edge case/manual review + readout.

I’ll include model config suggestions for Karthik once we align on expected token lengths (Maya, can you share median/95th token lengths?).

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Attachment referenced: redwood_alpha_test_checklist.xlsx (internal)

Appreciate the detail — this looks actionable. Confirming: Crestline agrees to Oct 12 kickoff and the two-week sandbox. Procurement will wait for the quote + SOW to release the PO; I’ll aim to get the labeled benchmark and median token stats to you by EOD Oct 8.

A couple of small asks from my side before kickoff: 
- Please include an example cost projection (3 scenarios: no cache, moderate cache, aggressive cache) with expected monthlyized run-rate extrapolated from the alpha.
- For the manual evaluation, can Redwood provide a simple annotation template so our SMEs can flag hallucination and partial-extraction cases consistently?

If you can send the quote/SOW + the cost projection and annotation template by Oct 9 we should be on track to start Oct 12. Looking forward to it.

Thanks —
Maya
Product Lead, Crestline AI
